Definition: genitive case compound of G1700 and G846; of myself so likewise the dative case ἐμαυτῷ, and accusative case ἐμαυτόν:--me, mine own (self), myself.
BiblicalUsage: emautoû means of myself. In Luke 7:7, the text says "Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee." In John 5:30, the text says "I can of mine own self do nothing."
TheologicalSignificance: What emautoû teaches me is that humility is not thinking less of ourselves; it is thinking of ourselves less, and of God more. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Centurion's Servant; Paul's Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
